title: Pay yourself first
principle: Set aside a fixed share of your income for your future self the moment it arrives, before any other spending happens. Treat that transfer like a bill you owe yourself, non-negotiable and automatic — the classic version of this advice comes from Clason's parables, and was later turned into an automated system by David Bach's The Automatic Millionaire, which argues the transfer should require no willpower because it happens without you having to decide each month.
formula: A fixed percentage of net income is reserved for savings first; needs and wants split whatever remains.
fitsWhen: You struggle to save whatever's left over at the end of the month and want saving to happen automatically instead of by discipline.
critique: A fixed percentage taken off the top can be unrealistic in months with unusually high essential costs, and it says nothing about how to size that percentage sensibly for your situation.
